subject: Recover discarded product-dimension features as brand-month signals
description:
Engineered matrix (30 cols, 2,552 rows) carries NO product attributes. dim_product has 20+ columns; aggregate reads exactly two (product_id, brand).

Raw SKU attributes cannot survive a brand-month groupby (FAXE KONDI = 7 sizes x 3 packaging over 144 SKUs), but they CAN survive as brand-month aggregates.

MEASURED correlation with sales_units at brand-month:
  n_skus_active   r = 0.848   <- beats lag_1 (0.585) and weighted_dist (0.756)
  n_sizes         r = 0.658
  n_packaging     r = 0.469
  n_variants      r = 0.424
  avg_pack_litres r = 0.289

CAVEAT 1 -- is it a size proxy? Big brands have more SKUs AND more sales. Compute the WITHIN-brand correlation (does a brand own SKU count moving predict its own sales moving?) before believing 0.848.

CAVEAT 2 -- needs shift(1) within group_keys, like promo_intensity in V3. This month SKU count is not known when forecasting this month.

CAVEAT 3 (Brian, deployment) -- a marketing manager will NOT know n_skus_active by heart when asking 'what are sales in 6 months?'. Resolution is a 3-tier policy, NOT user-supplied input:
  Tier 1 AUTO-DERIVE (default): the feature is a property of the brand own history, already in the feature matrix. The forecast service looks up history server-side (the SRQ2 design) and derives it exactly as it derives lag_1. User supplies nothing.
  Tier 2 USER OVERRIDE (optional): if the manager DOES know ('we are delisting 3 SKUs in Q3'), expose it as an optional typed tool parameter -> becomes a scenario/what-if feature. This turns the limitation into an SRQ2 capability: forecast-informed decision support.
  Tier 3 TRAINING AVERAGE: cold-start brands with no history only.

  OPEN PROBLEM for multi-step horizons: at h=6 the auto-derived value is the last known SKU count carried forward 6 months, degrading with horizon. Either (a) hold constant and document, (b) forecast it as a second series, or (c) restrict it to short horizons. Measure degradation by horizon before choosing. This is a genuine Ch10 limitation either way.

Also available as near-constant brand statics: manufacturer (99.7% constant within brand-month), category (100%), plus binary regular_light / organic / private_label / price_category.

NOTE (F20): Danskvand lacks promo columns entirely and RTD facts are EMPTY, so any new feature family must declare per-category availability rather than assume CSD schema.

Verify: within-brand correlation reported; horizon-degradation measured; if it survives, add lagged features and re-measure model performance with/without.
